citation.authors: Rucker Wright D, Gathers R, Kapke A, Johnson D et al
citation.journal: Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology

record.population: 201 caregivers of African American girls aged 1-15, US clinics
record.finding: Cornrows were associated with traction alopecia in the non-dermatology clinic group (adjusted odds ratio 5.79, 95% CI 1.35-24.8). For seborrhoeic dermatitis, extensions (odds ratio 2.37) and infrequent oil use (3.69) were associated; wash frequency was not. 99% used oils or grease, 80% hot combs, 42% chemical relaxers.
record.note: Caregiver report, small, wide confidence intervals; associations only.

record.population: 201 caregivers of African American girls aged 1-15, US clinics
record.finding: 99% reported using hair oils or grease. Infrequent hair oil use was associated with seborrheic dermatitis (adjusted odds ratio 3.69, 95% CI 1.07-12.7). No association was found between hair grease use and tinea capitis, or between washing frequency and either condition.
record.note: Small, caregiver-reported, cross-sectional, with a very wide confidence interval; it cannot show oil prevents the condition. Counted as a signal, not as evidence the practice works.
